request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Ledgerpoint
- Target role: Backend Engineer, Payments
- Seniority: mid
- Key skills to assess: Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, event-driven architectures, idempotency, exactly-once processing, observability, strangler-fig migrations, property-based testing
- Focus areas: payment systems, concurrency correctness, distributed systems, system reliability, data consistency

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.skill: Idempotency and exactly-once processing in payment systems
slots.intent: Assess understanding of how to prevent duplicate charges and ensure payment state consistency in a distributed, message-driven payment platform
key_points: Idempotency keys and request deduplication strategies
Exactly-once semantics vs. at-least-once delivery guarantees
Reconciliation patterns for detecting and handling missed or duplicate transactions
Database design choices (unique constraints, state tables) to enforce idempotency

slots.skill: Event-driven architecture with Kafka and PostgreSQL
slots.intent: Evaluate ability to design reliable payment event pipelines that maintain data consistency across multiple services and handle backpressure
key_points: Partition strategy for payment events (by merchant, customer, or transaction ID) and ordering guarantees
Outbox pattern or CDC to atomically write state changes and publish events
Consumer group management and offset tracking for reliable event replay
Handling schema evolution and version compatibility in payment event streams

slots.skill: Observability and debugging in distributed payment flows
slots.intent: Determine capability to instrument, monitor, and troubleshoot payment transactions across multiple services and identify root causes of failures or inconsistencies
key_points: Distributed tracing (trace IDs, span correlation) to follow a payment through multiple services
Metrics, logs, and alerts for detecting payment anomalies (stuck transactions, latency spikes)
Debugging techniques for race conditions and timing-dependent failures in concurrent payment processing
Observability trade-offs: sampling strategies and cost vs. fidelity in high-volume payment systems
